_comment: Mutations for the gitignore rules that keep a COPY of the live environment
file out of the PUBLIC repository.
E1: the HYPHEN separator rule `.env-*` is gone. Measured 2026-11-04 by the
review panel: `.env-backup`, `.env-copy` and `.env-20261103` matched
NEITHER `.env.*` NOR `.env_*` NOR `*.env`, so `git add -A` still swept
them into a public commit.
E2: the tracked-file guard no longer recognises `check.txt`. The guard
filters on basenames starting or ending with `.env`, so a tracked
`check.txt` -- which this diff newly ignores -- would become
un-addable with NOTHING guarding it. The guard is a named function
precisely so that this coverage is testable.
E3: the DOT separator rule `.env.*` is gone.
E4: the UNDERSCORE separator rule `.env_*` is gone.
E5: the negation is UNANCHORED again (`!.env.production`). The original
defect: it re-opened `.env.production` at EVERY level, including the
repository ROOT, where `deploy.sh:63` names it as one of the four
canonical live env filenames.
E6: the probe drops `--no-index`. WITHOUT it `git check-ignore` consults
the index first and reports every TRACKED path as 'not ignored' no
matter what the rules say -- so the whole suite would pass while
measuring nothing. The control test in the target file proves the
difference on a real tracked file, so this mutant cannot hide.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/gitignore_env_copies.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.
